title: PrivNet Guardian: Terraform module for VPC egress, SG/NACL, and private DNS controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: ship a single, opinionated Terraform module (privnet_guardian) that enforces VPC security controls for Private deployments: security groups (least-privilege defaults + role-scoped overrides), stateless NACL templates per-subnet class, private DNS (split-horizon hosted zones + resolver rules), and egress policy primitives (explicit allow-lists, deny-default, optional egress-proxy endpoint).

Scope and constraints:
- Support AWS first (VPC, SG, NACL, Route53 Resolver), with extension points for Azure/GCP later.
- Module should be consumable by both Redwood Private installs and customer on-prem tooling (clear inputs/outputs).
- Avoid creating cross-account resources by default; allow opt-in for shared resolver endpoints.
- Maintainable upgrade path: non-destructive defaults and explicit migration helpers for breaking changes.

Design decisions and API surface (high level):
- Inputs: env_tag, vpc_id, subnets (map by role: app|db|ingress), outbound_allowlist (list of CIDRs or service tags), egress_proxy (optional ALB/NLB endpoint + CIDR), dns_private_zone_map (domain -> hosted_zone_id), resolver_rules (list), enable_vpc_flow_logs (bool), enable_audit_nacls (bool).
- Outputs: security_group_ids, nacl_ids, resolver_endpoint_id, resolver_rule_ids, module_version.
- Security Groups: provide three base modules (app, infra, bastion) with minimal open ports and a pattern for role-bound augmentation (module consumer passes extra ingress sources per role).
- NACLs: template-based policies with explicit ephemeral port allowances for ephemeral clusters; deny-by-default rule at higher priority to prevent accidental wide-open egress.
- DNS: create private hosted zones when requested, configure Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints for hybrid DNS, and create resolver rules with priority. Include optional split-horizon templates for customer domains.
- Egress policy: default-deny for outbound to internet; explicit allowlist for known services; optional egress-proxy pattern where traffic is routed through a dedicated subnet+proxy (recommended for tight compliance).

Upgrade & migration strategy:
- Semantic versioning of module; breaking changes require major version bump and documented migration steps.
- Provide terraform scripts for in-place state move (terraform state mv/import helpers) and a test harness to run in a staging VPC.
- CI pipeline policy: all major bumps trigger a dry-run-only integration in a disposable account and a canary apply to one non-prod VPC (canary subnet tag).
- Backwards compatibility shims: where possible keep old outputs and create new ones; deprecate over two releases.

Health checks and observability:
- Preflight: terraform validate + terraform plan conformance checks + tfsec/Checkov static checks in CI.
- Runtime: enable VPC Flow Logs to a central S3 + Athena for queries and to CloudWatch Logs for dashboards.
- Synthetic canaries: a small Lambda (or container) that initiates DNS resolution and HTTP egress to allowlist targets on a schedule; failures produce PagerDuty alerts.
- Drift detection: periodic terraform plan runs against managed VPCs (scheduled via GitHub Actions / Atlantis) and alerts for drift > X resources.
- Health signals: SG/NACL misconfig changes, Route53 resolver endpoint status, high rate of rejected connections. Wire to Console dashboards and per-customer alerting channels.

Acceptance criteria (top-level):
- Module accepts inputs described above and produces deterministic outputs.
- CI gates (validate, plan, tfsec) pass for example staging VPC manifest.
- Canary deploy validates DNS resolution and egress path in staging.
- Module docs and example overlays for Common, PCI, and HIPAA patterns published.
- Security review completed and checklist signed off.

Operational runbook (short):
- How to rollback: revert Terraform to last known-good module version and apply; if resource requires import, run provided import script.
- Nightly checks: drift-report, resolver-endpoint-health, VPC flow anomaly scan.
- Emergency steps: attach temporary SG allowing diagnostics from jump-host CIDR, preserve logs, engage infra on-call.

Notes on implementation approach:
- Use small, composable submodules (sg_base, nacl_base, dns_resolver, egress_proxy) published under module registry path redwood-inference/privnet_guardian/aws.
- Prefer explicit resource names and tags for easier state migrations.
- Provide examples for Atlantis and GitHub Actions automations (plan comment parsing and apply gating).

Expected owners: infra-sre + private-deploy infra team. Security to review ACL templates before merge.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module builds (terraform init) and applies in staging without manual state edits; 2) Synthetic canary passes DNS + egress checks for three allowlist targets; 3) CI static checks (tfsec/Checkov) show zero critical failures; 4) Documentation + example manifests published; 5) Security review sign-off recorded in PR.
